newsitem.title: INDIA: Top India court stays arrest of politician - agency.
newsitem.headline: Top India court stays arrest of politician - agency.

text.p: India's Supreme Court on Friday ordered that the chief minister of the eastern state of Bihar not be arrested until it had heard his plea against detention, the Press Trust of India (PTI) news agency said.

The order by the nation's top court was issued shortly after a special investigative court in the Bihar state capital of Patna issued arrest warrants against Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav and three other politicians in connection with a $280 million corruption scandal.

PTI said a three-judge bench of the Supreme Court said Yadav could not be arrested until it had heard his appeal against a Bihar court's order on Thursday rejecting his plea for anticipatory bail, allowed under Indian law to people who anticipate possible arrest.

The Supreme Court order renewed the see-saw controversy over Yadav, a charismatic politician who has stubbornly refused to step down despite his indictment by federal police in the corruption scandal in which 56 politicians and officials have been named for the alleged use of fictitious firms to milk state funds.

India's Parliament has been rocked by angry debate over Yadav since its monsoon session began on Wednesday. The crisis has divided leaders of the country's ruling coalition who are arguing over whether or not to retain Yadav's group in their fold.
The Yadav news shook up India's premier Bombay Stock Exchange, which fell sharply but then recovered some ground to stand 33.58 points or 0.79 percent down at 4192.99 at 0925 GMT.
